key_insight: Wind shear and veer can cut actuator-disk power efficiency by more than 20% because their effects are not only geometric but also change induction and rotor aerodynamics.
engineering_relevance: Turbine power prediction models should account for shear, veer, and wall proximity because inductive losses can be a major part of real ABL performance degradation.
method: Concurrent-precursor LES of an actuator-disk wind turbine in stratified atmospheric boundary layer conditions
Controlled inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently
Decomposition of losses into geometric rotor-equivalent wind-speed effects and inductive aerodynamic effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that simulated shear and veer conditions reduced power coefficient by more than 20%, with inductive effects explaining a significant fraction of the loss.
watch_item: The conclusions come from actuator-disk LES and simplified inflow cases, so translating them directly to full-blade turbines and complex terrain may require additional validation.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
